title: Game notation adapter: human-readable move input/output
description:
Support established game notations (chess algebraic, Go SGF coordinates, etc.) in the REPL and CLI. Declarative JSON for common patterns, WASM escape hatch for exotic notation.

## Two layers

### Layer 1: Generic label-based coordinates (automatic, zero config)
Game definitions already declare grid labels:
```json
"labels": {"files": ["a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h"], "ranks": [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]}
```
Map "e4" to "4,3" via label lookup. Works for any game with labeled grids.

### Layer 2: Declarative notation spec (in game definition JSON)
Most notation systems decompose into a template + symbols + disambiguation + special moves:
```json
"notation": {
  "piece_symbols": {"king": "K", "queen": "Q", "rook": "R", "bishop": "B", "knight": "N", "pawn": ""},
  "capture_marker": "x",
  "disambiguation": "file_then_rank",
  "special_moves": {
    "O-O": {"action_type": "castle", "side": "kingside"},
    "O-O-O": {"action_type": "castle", "side": "queenside"}
  },
  "promotion_marker": "=",
  "check_marker": "+"
}
```

Disambiguation is resolved against the legal move list — "which legal move targeting this square matches the hint?" The engine already enumerates legal moves, so disambiguation is just filtering.

Covers: chess algebraic, shogi, xiangqi, and most piece-on-grid games without any code.

### Layer 3: WASM escape hatch (for exotic notation)
Notation that cannot be expressed declaratively (context-dependent parsing beyond disambiguation, non-grid games, etc.) can be implemented as a WASM module exporting:
- parse(text, state_json) -> action_json
- format(action_json, state_json) -> text

Same WASM module runs in browser client, terminal client, and server. Uses the existing WASM infrastructure (wasm-bindgen, wasmtime).

## Implementation options by platform

| Layer | Where it runs | Implementation |
|-------|--------------|----------------|
| Label mapping | Everywhere | Read grid labels from definition |
| Declarative spec | Everywhere | JSON in definition, engine parses |
| Python plugin | REPL, CLI, bots | Dev convenience, mirrors declarative spec |
| WASM module | Browser, server, native | Portable, same code all platforms |

## Games covered by declarative spec (no code needed)
- Chess: piece symbols + file_then_rank disambiguation + castling/promotion special moves
- Go: label mapping only (letter coordinates, "pass" as special move)
- Shogi: piece symbols + rank_then_file disambiguation + drop notation
- Xiangqi: piece symbols + file-based disambiguation
- Backgammon: point numbers as labels + bar/off special positions
- Card games: component type names as notation (no grid, just names)

## Games needing WASM escape hatch
- Games with computed notation (e.g. notation depends on game-specific scoring)
- Games with non-standard disambiguation rules
- Historical notation formats (descriptive chess notation)

## Schema additions
- Optional "notation" object in game-definition.schema.json
- piece_symbols: map of component type to display character
- capture_marker, promotion_marker, check_marker: string
- disambiguation: "file_then_rank" | "rank_then_file" | "none"
- special_moves: map of notation string to action dict
- wasm_notation: optional WASM module name for exotic notation
close_reason: Notation adapter complete: notation.py module, schema, Chess SAN, Go, TTT, Cube Singmaster, Backgammon, Carcassonne. 39 tests total.
